newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila underwriters seek to revive IPO allocations.
newsitem.headline: Manila underwriters seek to revive IPO allocations.

text.p: The Investment Houses Association of the Philippines (IHAP) said on Monday it wanted to revive the 10 percent mandatory allocation of initial public offerings (IPO) to small retail investors.
The mandatory allocation was implemented last year but was discontinued later due to lacklustre demand from small investors.
Small investors are those buying shares worth less than 10,000 pesos.
In the new scheme submitted to the Securities and Exchange Commission, IHAP, which represents underwriters, said application forms can be availed through newspapers.
The mandatory allocation will help deepen the capital market, IHAP president Roberto Atendido said.
"Our IPOs have not been really made available to the general public at large, but rather to the favoured public," Atendido told reporters.
Under the proposed scheme, 30 percent of the IPO will be set aside for institutional investors and 60 percent to be distributed by the underwriter syndicates.
At present, 50 percent of the IPO are automatically set aside for the member-brokers of the Philipine Stock Exchange, while the rest are distributed by the underwriters.
